summary: Queue a job. `input` is the application's own and the server never reads it; the application's build hook turns it into the request when the job's turn comes - which is after every job in `after` has landed, so a job can be built from its predecessors' actual output. With the default hooks the request is `input` itself. A text model takes a prompt - a string, or `{"prompt": ...}`, sent as one user message - or a conversation, the contract's `conversation` shape: `{"messages": [{"role": "system" | "user" | "assistant", "content": ...}, ...]}`, a system message and the turns before this one, sent as they were built, in their order. Any other request - a role no chat template takes, a conversation carrying anything more - fails its job before a model is loaded or asked, in the validator's words. A whisper model's request is audio, the contract's `audio_request`: `{"audio": <a WAV file on the server's machine>, "fields": {...}}` - every field whisper-server 1.9.1 reads, each optional, each of the kind it reads it as, and `response_format` the engine's own, as it asks for the verbose answer. With the default hooks, where the request is the job's `input`, a job for a whisper model is checked AT SUBMIT: an input that is not such a request - a field whisper-server does not read, which it would ignore without a word, one of the wrong kind, `response_format`, or no audio at all - is refused `bad_audio_request`, never sent; with an application's own hooks the request is checked when it is built, and one that is not such a request fails its job before a model is loaded, as does a WAV that cannot be read. `group` names a fan and `group_size` says how many members it will have: a fan settles once that many exist and every one has ended, and without a size its first member could land before its second was submitted. `scope` is a key of the application's own - a book, a project - that listing and pruning can be narrowed to. `gen` is the request's parameters. Three are the queue's own: `model`, `n` (how many answers, each asked on its own with its own seed) and `retries` (how often an attempt the application's judge refused is asked again; 0 turns retries off). Every other one is a parameter llama-server's chat route reads that is the application's to set - llama-server b10724, as its source reads a request - each optional, and each sent to the model exactly as it was named: the samplers (`temperature`, `top_k`, `top_p`, `min_p`, `samplers` and the rest), how long the answer may be (`max_tokens`) and where it stops (`stop`), a JSON schema or a grammar that forces the answer's shape (`json_schema`, `grammar`, `response_format`), the prompt cache (`cache_prompt`, `n_cache_reuse`, `id_slot`), a limit on thinking (`reasoning_budget_tokens`, `reasoning_budget_message`), and the template's own switches (`chat_template_kwargs`, `reasoning_effort`, `add_generation_prompt`, `continue_final_message`). A parameter this list does not name is refused `bad_request`, never ignored - a misspelt one never reaches the model - and so is one of the wrong kind; what a value means is llama-server's to judge, and a value it refuses fails the job in its own words. Where the application names nothing, the model's own settings apply (its `temperature`, `top_p`, `min_p` and `repeat_penalty`, and no thinking for a model its settings tell not to think), then the bootstrap's (`max_tokens` 600), then llama-server's. `max_tokens` -1 names no limit: the answer may run to the end of the model's context; 0 reads the prompt into the cache and asks for no answer, so an empty one does not fail the job. The sampling an application's hook chooses may name the model's parameters, never the queue's own three: a hook that names `model`, `n` or `retries` fails the job, because the job's record names what it runs. At the job's turn, with its model up and before the model is asked, the request is counted by the model - rendered with its own chat template, counted by its own tokenizer - against the context the model says it has: the prompt and the room its answer needs (its `max_tokens`, and at least one token) must fit, or the job ends `failed` with the `reason` `prompt_too_long`, its `error` saying the three numbers - never cut to fit. The count is on the job, as `progress.count`. `gen.seed` fixes the first attempt's seed: every later attempt moves it, so a retry is never a replay. A body missing `kind` or `gen.model` is answered by `no_kind` or `no_model`; any other way it does not match this request is `bad_request`, naming the first problem. `correlation_id` names this request everywhere it goes. The client that starts a request mints it; a request that comes without one is given one by the server, and `correlation_source` says which - so a record never claims a client id it was not sent. A client's id already taken in this folder is refused `correlation_taken`: one id naming two requests would join two records into one. `client` is the asking client's actor id, recorded on the job so a client can find its own work. A JOB THAT DOES NOT SAY IT IS BATCH IS LIVE (PLAN-4 D0: the class's default is responsive): without `priority` a job is `interactive`, and only `priority: batch`, said by the application, makes it scheduled work. `priority` is the job's place in the queue's order - an `interactive` job goes before every `batch` one, then first come first served - and also its class when it waits for the card: an `interactive` job asks the coordinator as `responsive`, a `batch` one as `scheduled`. So a job that names no priority goes before batch work, asks as `responsive`, never waits for room, and can name neither a `not_before` still to come nor `if_no_room: wait`. `card_patience_s` is how long this job waits for the card - the application's choice, per request; without it, the server's own (`card_patience_s` in its runner settings, an hour unless set there), and 0 means now or not at all. A job whose patience runs out ends `failed` with a `reason` of its own, `card_patience`; one that would not wait and found the card busy, `card_busy` - and neither names who has the card; one whose request does not fit its model's context, `prompt_too_long`. `check: true` marks a job to be checked before it is sent (PLAN-4 D16): once its request is built, at its turn, it waits `held` - with the exact request as it would be sent, `GET /api/jobs/{id}/held` - until a person sends it, as built or changed for this one request (`POST /api/jobs/{id}/send`), or cancels it; the job says `check`: `marked`, `held`, then `sent` or `tuned`. A job not marked never waits for anyone, and `check` is not on it. A patience below 0 is refused `bad_patience`. SCHEDULED WORK (S18, the owner's second ruling of 2026-09-28): a `batch` job whose model does not fit on the card when its turn comes either waits for room - within its patience - or fails at once, `no_room`, in the loud words a live job does: `if_no_room`, `wait` or `fail`, says which for this job; without it, the server's own (`scheduled_if_no_room` in its runner settings, `wait` unless set there). Waiting, it goes back to the queue - `queued`, holding back nobody, its `progress` saying what it waits for in words and numbers (`waiting_for`, `free_mib`, `need_mib`, `outside_mib`, `waited_s`, `patience_left_s`) - and runs by itself the first moment its model fits; a patience that runs out while it waits fails it `no_room`, in those loud words, saying how long it waited. `not_before` is the time - seconds since the epoch, as every other time here - a `batch` job starts no earlier than: until then it is `queued` and holds back nobody - every other job goes first, and the card is not asked for it - and from its time it starts the first moment it can, its model fitting; its patience counts from its time (from the first look at the queue after it, so a machine that slept through the time starts it when it wakes). A time already past is now. A job that is not `batch` - `interactive`, said or not - is live, and live work is now: one that names a `not_before` still to come, or `if_no_room: wait`, is refused `live_is_now`, its words saying that `priority: batch` is what lets a job wait. A `max_tokens` llama-server refuses - below -1, or above 2147483647 - is refused `bad_max_tokens`, and never sent; so is one an application's sampling hook chooses, whose job fails before its model is asked. Every other parameter llama-server holds to hard limits (b10724) is held to them here as well - `n_keep` and `reasoning_budget_tokens` from -1, `n_indent`, `n_discard`, `n_cache_reuse`, `repeat_last_n`, `dry_allowed_length`, `dry_penalty_last_n` and `min_keep` from 0, each up to 2147483647; `t_max_predict_ms` from -1 up to 9223372036854775807; `adaptive_decay` from 0 to 0.99 - and a value outside them is refused `out_of_range`, its `error` naming the parameter, its range and the value, and never sent; so is one a sampling hook chooses.
